title: Top three scores
scenario: Five scores on the board. Which three are the biggest?

intro.job: Five scores on the board. Which three are the biggest?

idea.rule: Sort first, then slice — the first three are the biggest three.
idea.detail: Two patterns chained: sorting (013) puts the scores in order; slicing (006) takes the first three. The draft slices before sorting, so it takes the first three in shelf order — 12, 45 and 8 — instead of the three biggest.

model_restatement: Take the three biggest scores — and print them.

clarify.question: What if two scores tie?
clarify.answer: Not today — the top three are distinct.

clarify.question: Why sort first?
clarify.answer: Slicing takes the first three in whatever order the list is in — sort first so the first three are the biggest.

clarify.question: Why three?
clarify.answer: The board shows the top three — change [:3] to take a different count.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Sort the scores biggest first. Take the first three. Print them.

checkpoints.prompt: On the print line, what is top?
With the fix — after line 1, what is top?

why_line: The draft takes the first three scores in shelf order — 12, 45, 8 — before sorting, so the biggest scores on the board never get in.

explain.rule: Slicing takes what the list hands it — [:3] is the first three in the order they sit, not the three biggest.
explain.bridge: What does [:3] take — the three biggest, or the first three in the order they sit?

fix.rule: Sort biggest-first, then slice: sorted(scores, reverse=True)[:3].

walk.gloss: Sort the scores biggest first — the list is in trophy order.
Take the first three — now they are the biggest three.

alternatives.note: Sort smallest-first, take the last three, flip them — same top three.

hints: What order are the scores in when you slice?
Sorting lines them up — slice after the sort.
top = sorted(scores, reverse=True)[:3] — then print it.

follow_up.prompt: One more board: [30, 10, 50, 20, 40] — which three are the biggest?

checkpoint.prompt: With the new board, what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — sorting puts the biggest first, whatever the scores are.

one_liner: Sort first, then slice — the first three are the biggest three.
